attributes.title: Level 2

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using dot operators in your code to access the properties of a function or object, and using code comments to make your code easier to read.

questions.hint: What should you look for to find the property in a line of JavaScript code?
questions.title: [Select one] What is the property in effects.blizzard.startScreenEffect(duration, particlesPerSecond)?
questions.correctResponse: A property is an element of code that belongs to a sprite or special object, such as an effect.

questions.hint: What do you use to add parameters to code in the JavaScript editor?
questions.title: [Select one] Typing out code in the JavaScript editor allows coders access to more parameters than the blocks editor.
questions.correctResponse: The JavaScript editor has many more parameter options to customize what the code is doing.

questions.hint: What symbol indicates a dot operator in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one] What is a dot operator?

answers.text: A nickname for your friend Dorothy
A spot on your computer screen
A symbol that is used in the middle of a line of code to add properties

questions.correctResponse: A dot operator is used to add properties and functions to objects in a program.

questions.hint: What will happen when a computer program reads text following //?
questions.title:
[Select one] What do you call a line of JavaScript text that starts with //?

﻿
questions.correctResponse: A comment is a line of code that starts with // and is skipped over when the program runs.

questions.title: [Open response] Why is it helpful to use comments in your code?
questions.correctResponse: Those sound like great ideas! Excited to see how you use comments in JavaScript in Blue Belt!

subgroups.title: Properties and Code Comments!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using dot operators in your code to access the properties of a function or object, and using code comments to make your code easier to read.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 2 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about properties and code comments. In JavaScript, you can type directly on the editor to organize your code using code comments and set different sprite properties. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 2:

badges.title: Parameter Pilot
badges.description: Use the JavaScript editor’s documentation and code completion tools when adding parameters to functions.

badges.title: Comment, Like, and Subscribe
badges.description: Add a comment to your code.

badges.title: Say What Now?
badges.description: Use the sayText function with all 5 parameters.

badges.title: Stop and Smell the Roses
badges.description: Use the pause function to temporarily stop your project from running new code.

badges.title: Effective Immediately
badges.description: Use the startScreenEffect function with 2 parameters.

badges.title: Music to My Ears
badges.description: Use the play function to play a melody.

badges.title: To Whom it May Concern
badges.description: Use the splash function to display a message on screen.

badges.title: A Speedy Recovery
badges.description: Set a sprite’s velocity property without using the setVelocity function.

badges.title: Wall of Text
badges.description: Use the showLongText function with 2 parameters.
